rights.redistributed_content: Original example code, pack-designed input states, independently evaluated numerical results and a small attributed selection of fundamental-constant facts. No source PDF, database dump, source image, proprietary result or source prose is included.
rights.rationale: Published equations and selected physical-constant facts are used to create new reference calculations. This is not a claim that all NRL/NIST publications or databases have an unrestricted redistribution licence.

deuteron_mass.status: CODATA 2022 central value; bare nucleus, not neutral atom

vacuum_permeability.status: CODATA 2022 central value; not assumed exactly 4*pi*1e-7

constant_policy: Published rounded central values are frozen independently; epsilon0*mu0*c^2 is therefore unity only to the precision of those published numbers. Source standard uncertainties are not numerical regression tolerances and no uncertainty propagation is claimed.
input_origin: Three explicitly chosen analytic verification states; not measured data or parameter estimates from any device.
si_conversion: Use charge in coulombs, density in m^-3, mass in kg, B in tesla, E in V/m and thermal energy kB*T = e*T_eV joules. Gaussian electrostatic factors 4*pi become 1/epsilon0; magnetic inertia uses mu0. No rounded Gaussian practical coefficient is treated as a high precision SI coefficient.

independence.subject: derive_values.py uses binary64 and never reads frozen values or independent_reference.py.
independence.frozen_reference: reference_values.json was computed separately using 60-digit Decimal arithmetic in independent_reference.py, then rounded to JSON binary64-representable decimal numbers. The verifier independently transcribes constants/states and uses rearranged algebra; it has no write option.
independence.limitation: Two implementations and source review reduce transcription/arithmetic risk but are not an experimental comparison or proof of model applicability.

tolerance_policy.purpose: Cross-platform binary64 reproduction of explicitly rounded constants and public equations. Does not represent physical/model uncertainty, measurement precision or confidence interval.

applicability: Homogeneous fully ionized singly charged deuterium, ne=nD; isotropic Maxwellian temperature interpretation.
Electron Debye length is the electron-only screening contribution, not combined electron-ion screening.
Angular frequencies are radians per second, not cycles per second. Cyclotron quantity is positive magnitude.
Thermal speed is sqrt(kB*Ti/md), a one-dimensional Maxwellian standard deviation. Gyroradius is the matching characteristic scale; not perpendicular-RMS gyroradius.

Alfven speed is ideal nonrelativistic MHD with ion mass density; electron inertia, displacement-current, finite-Larmor-radius, kinetic and anisotropy corrections omitted. Wave use additionally requires long wavelengths and frequencies small compared with ion gyrofrequency.
Total beta uses scalar electron plus ion thermal pressure and magnetic pressure B^2/(2*mu0); no stability threshold is asserted.
E-cross-B drift assumes uniform steady crossed fields and collisionless magnetized guiding-center motion; selected drift speeds are nonrelativistic.
Plasma frequencies and electron inertial length are classical characteristic scales, not a complete magnetized dispersion relation.
No universal model-error bound is supplied. Compare to simulation only after matching conventions and the required ordering.
